title: The Latest: Joe Biden Takes Command

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: The 2020 race to the Democratic nomination is now essentially down to a two-man contest between former Vice President Joe Biden and Senator Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 2020 年民主党总统候选人提名的竞选现在基本上缩小为前副总统乔·拜登和参议员伯尼·桑德斯之间的两人对决。

sentences.en: There are six states holding primary elections today.
sentences.zh: 今天有六个州举行初选。

sentences.en: Out of those six states, Michigan holding the most delegates, 125.
sentences.zh: 在这六个州中，密歇根州拥有的代表人数最多，为 125 人。

sentences.en: Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, North Dakota, Idaho, Washington State, you will be heard.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州、密西西比州、密苏里州、北达科他州、爱达荷州、华盛顿州，你们的声音将被听到。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, there is going to be a very, very important primary here in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 周二，密歇根州将举行一场非常非常重要的初选。

sentences.en: Michigan could be a make-or-break moment for Sanders.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州可能是决定桑德斯成败的关键时刻。

sentences.en: Do you see it that way?
sentences.zh: 你是这么看的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Michigan, I'm counting on you in a big way.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州，我对你们寄予厚望。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Alex Burns in New York.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是亚历克斯·伯恩斯，在纽约发来报道。

sentences.en: We've just had another big election night and another major breakthrough for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚迎来了又一个盛大的选举之夜，这也是乔·拜登取得的又一次重大突破。

sentences.en: The Democratic primary campaign moved to six new states on
sentences.zh: 民主党初选竞选活动于周二

sentences.en: Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 转移到了六个新州。

sentences.en: And the question was whether Biden would keep the momentum he gained on Super Tuesday or
sentences.zh: 问题在于拜登是会保持他在“超级星期二”获得的气势，

sentences.en: whether Bernie Sanders would make a comeback of his own, most of all in Michigan, where Sanders won a stunning upset against Hillary Clinton four years ago.
sentences.zh: 还是伯尼·桑德斯会实现自我翻盘，最重要的是在密歇根州——四年前桑德斯曾在这里击败希拉里·克林顿，爆出惊天冷门。

sentences.en: It is 9 p.m.
sentences.zh: 东海岸时间晚上 9 点，

sentences.en: on the East Coast and polls are now closed just about.
sentences.zh: 投票刚刚基本结束。

sentences.en: As results rolled in, it became clear that it was Biden's night.
sentences.zh: 随着结果不断出炉，很明显这是属于拜登的夜晚。

sentences.en: He won and he won decisively in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 他在密歇根州赢了，而且赢得毫不含糊。

sentences.en: NBC News can now project that Joe Biden is going to win the state of Michigan, as you can see.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，美国全国广播公司新闻网（NBC News）现在预测乔·拜登将赢得密歇根州。

sentences.en: In Missouri.
sentences.zh: 在密苏里州。

sentences.en: With some breaking news, ABC News can now project Joe Biden will win the Missouri Democratic primary here.
sentences.zh: 根据突发新闻，美国广播公司新闻网（ABC News）现在预测乔·拜登将赢得密苏里州民主党初选。

sentences.en: This is a huge win.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: And in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 在密西西比州。

sentences.en: CBS News projects former Vice President Joe Biden will win the primary in
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻网（CBS News）预测前副总统乔·拜登将赢得

sentences.en: Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的初选。

sentences.en: He won on the strength of a multiracial coalition that has propelled his national resurgence
sentences.zh: 他凭借多元种族联盟的力量获胜，正是这个联盟推动了他在过去三周内的全国复苏，

sentences.en: over the last three weeks, a coalition that has combined some of the Democratic Party's most loyal
sentences.zh: 这个联盟将民主党一些最忠实的选民

sentences.en: voters, including African-Americans and women with newer arrivals, including moderate white voters who have fled Donald Trump's Republican Party.
sentences.zh: （包括非裔美国人和女性）与新加入者（包括逃离唐纳德·特朗普的共和党的温和派白人选民）结合在了一起。

sentences.en: At this point, Biden's political campaign has come full circle from frontrunner to underdog to frontrunner again and now very likely the future Democratic presidential nominee.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，拜登的政治竞选经历了完整的轮回：从领跑者到落后者，再到重新领跑，现在很有可能成为未来民主党总统候选人。

sentences.en: But the latest is that Sanders political base from 2016, the one that made him such a powerful challenger to Hillary Clinton has really broken apart.
sentences.zh: 但最新情况是，桑德斯 2016 年的政治基础——那个让他成为希拉里·克林顿强劲挑战者的基础——已经彻底瓦解了。

sentences.en: Here's the situation.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的。

sentences.en: If you take a look at all these states, Bernie Sanders barely lost Missouri last time.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看所有这些州，伯尼·桑德斯上次在密苏里州仅以微弱劣势落败。

sentences.en: He only was down one delegate when Missouri was done.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州结果出来时，他只落后一个代表名额。

sentences.en: That's not going to be the case tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚情况可就不同了。

sentences.en: He looks like he's going to lose it in a very big way.
sentences.zh: 他看起来要惨败了。

sentences.en: He lost Mississippi in a very big way.
sentences.zh: 他在密西西比州惨败。

sentences.en: The other three states are going to be very close.
sentences.zh: 另外三个州的竞争将会非常激烈。

sentences.en: He blew out Hillary Clinton by 40 points in each of those three states.
sentences.zh: 四年前他在那三个州分别以 40 个百分点的优势大胜希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: And so he still has strong support from young people and very liberal voters.
sentences.zh: 因此他仍然拥有来自年轻人和极自由派选民的强力支持。

sentences.en: But his support from working class white voters and rural whites really evaporated on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 但他在周二失去了工人阶级白人选民和农村白人选民的大力支持。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is leading among white voters in the state.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在该州的白人选民中领先。

sentences.en: That's where
sentences.zh: 这正是

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders won in 2016.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯在 2016 年获胜的地方。

sentences.en: Kalamazoo, home of western Michigan, basically all in right now.
sentences.zh: 卡拉马祖，西密歇根大学的所在地，现在基本上全线支持了。

sentences.en: Here's Bernie
sentences.zh: 这是伯尼·

sentences.en: Sanders barely hanging on a one point margin.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯以一个百分点的微弱优势艰难支撑。

sentences.en: Again, four years ago, this was a landslide.
sentences.zh: 同样，四年前这里曾是一场压倒性的胜利。

sentences.en: Sanders had argued that he could drive up turnout among progressives and again win over rural midwesterners as he did in 2016.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯曾辩称，他可以提高进步派的投票率，并像在 2016 年那样再次赢得中西部农村选民的支持。

sentences.en: But that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但那并没有发生。

sentences.en: A working class vote, a blue collar vote.
sentences.zh: 工人阶级的选票，蓝领的选票。

sentences.en: And as we've been talking about all night, that was really the vote that that propelled him to victory four years ago in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 正如我们整晚一直在讨论的那样，正是这张选票在四年前推动他在密歇根州走向胜利。

sentences.en: And to see that Joe Biden come in and start to eat away at the Sanders voters, white working class voters included, is a devastating blow to Bernie Sanders' campaign.
sentences.zh: 看到乔·拜登进来并开始蚕食桑德斯的选民（包括白人工人阶级选民），这对伯尼·桑德斯的竞选活动是一个毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: In fact, Biden routed Sanders across the countryside in Michigan and Missouri.
sentences.zh: 事实上，拜登在密歇根州和密苏里州的乡镇地区击溃了桑德斯。

sentences.en: So we're starting to see a bigger picture here of Democratic primary voters kind of starting to really align behind Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开始看到一幅更大的画面，即民主党初选选民开始真正团结在乔·拜登身后。

sentences.en: And you saw in our exit polling too, the things that they care about are electability.
sentences.zh: 正如你在我们的出口民调中所看到的，他们关心的核心是当选可能性。

sentences.en: So Sanders' struggle is not just about losing specific states.
sentences.zh: 因此，桑德斯的困境不仅仅是失去几个特定的州。

sentences.en: It's about seeing his theory of how to build a progressive majority put to the test and so far seeing it fail.
sentences.zh: 而是他关于如何建立进步派多数派的理论经受了考验，而到目前为止却宣告失败。

sentences.en: It really undercuts
sentences.zh: 这确实削弱了

sentences.en: Sanders' claim that only a candidate like him, who trumpets far reaching change, a political revolution, can energize the voters Democrats need to win.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯的断言，即只有像他这样高调宣扬深远变革、一场政治革命的候选人，才能激发民主党获胜所需的选民。

sentences.en: So now it's up to Joe Biden to show he can excite the voters who Bernie Sanders did bring into the party.
sentences.zh: 所以现在轮到乔·拜登来证明他能够激励伯尼·桑德斯曾经争取到党内的那些选民。

sentences.en: And I want to thank Bernie Sanders and his supporters for their tireless energy and their passion.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢伯尼·桑德斯和他的支持者们，感谢他们不知疲倦的精力和热情。

sentences.en: You heard Biden deliver a plea for unity on Tuesday night and tell Sanders voters we share a common goal.
sentences.zh: 你听到拜登在周二晚上发表了呼吁团结的恳求，并告诉桑德斯的支持者，我们有着共同的目标。

sentences.en: They shared a common goal of defeating Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们有着击败唐纳德·特朗普的共同目标。

sentences.en: We need you.
sentences.zh: 我们需要你们。

sentences.en: We want you.
sentences.zh: 我们欢迎你们。

sentences.en: And there's a place in our campaign for each of you.
sentences.zh: 我们的竞选团队中为你们每个人都留有位置。

sentences.en: But it's an open question whether young people will ever embrace Biden the way they have embraced
sentences.zh: 但年轻人是否会像拥抱桑德斯那样、像继续拥抱桑德斯那样去拥抱拜登，仍然是一个未知数，而且如果拜登被提名，伯尼·

sentences.en: Sanders, the way they continue to embrace Sanders, and if Biden is nominated, how much help Bernie
sentences.zh: 桑德斯能给他提供多少帮助也是个未知数。

sentences.en: Sanders might give him.
sentences.zh: 但是胜利意味着，但是胜利意味着团结美国，而不是播种更多的主分裂和愤怒。

sentences.en: But winning means, but winning means uniting America, not sowing more division and anger.
sentences.zh: 这意味着拥有一位不仅懂得如何战斗，更懂得如何治愈的总统。

sentences.en: It means having a president who not only knows how to fight, but knows how to heal.
sentences.zh: 这就是最新情况。

sentences.en: So that's the lateSt. For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎进了一群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人热血沸腾的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）共同主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在途中失去控制的故事。
